All 5 that exist are genuinely closed (and the epic's close reason matches the run), so this is a count/typo overstatement, not a fabricated closure — but the stated range is disproven by the tracker itself. Note the beads store lives in the main repo's .beads/embeddeddolt and is untracked in the reviewed worktree, so no reader of the tracked repo can verify this line at all.

The doc is internally inconsistent: the same Corrections section lists exactly five commits (F6c/F6f/F6e/F6a/F6b) and the epic's close reason names the same five. The finding's characterization (count/typo overstatement, not fabricated closure; five real children genuinely closed) is accurate, and the claim sits inside the post-audit corrections diff under review, so the report-honesty lens applies. The worktree indeed has no .beads directory, confirming the reviewer's verifiability caveat. Refutation attempts (charitable reading of the range, deleted-issue history, alternate store) all fail.

confirmed.claim: SECURITY.md F6e residual bullet: "the empty `empty.npmrc` is re-established at EVERY point of use — pipeline init and the executor `$npm` injection, immediately before the isolation flags are appended" (the dash-clause as an enumeration of the re-establishment points).
confirmed.problem: The enumeration contradicts the code in both slots it names. (1) "pipeline init" (apps/cli/src/pipeline.ts:102) is workspace CREATION, not a point of use: no --userconfig is consumed there and no "isolation flags" are appended nearby, so the qualifier "immediately before the isolation flags are appended" is false for it. (2) The code's second true point of use — the treeHash npm-ls install-observation path — is omitted entirely: apps/cli/src/pipeline.ts:597 re-establishes the file and :601 consumes it via '--userconfig', and the in-code comment at :594 ("same re-establish contract as the executor install path") shows the author treated it as a distinct third site. The umbrella assertion "re-established at EVERY point of use" survives the sweep (repo-wide grep of packages/runner/*/src and apps/*/src finds exactly two --userconfig consumers, :764 and :601, each with an immediately-preceding writeFileSync('empty.npmrc','')), so this is an under-claim/mislabel of locations, not a false protection claim — but a reader auditing the doc against the code will find a named site that is not a point of use and a real point of use that is unnamed.
confirmed.evidence: docs/SECURITY.md:96-98 (bullet text); apps/cli/src/pipeline.ts:102 (creation write, no flags appended); apps/cli/src/pipeline.ts:594-597,601 (unnamed re-establish + consumption in treeHash); packages/runner/executor/src/index.ts:761,763-766 (named re-establish + suffix flags, order --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --legacy-peer-deps --userconfig <path> --cache <path> --registry <pin>); grep sweep of userconfig/empty.npmrc over production src shows only these sites.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced; the finding's two factual sub-claims both check out against the code in this worktree, and it is not the disallowed "ceiling" complaint (the finding itself concedes the umbrella protection claim survives — it is a docs-semantics enumeration defect, and SECURITY.md is part of the corrections diff under review, so it is in scope).

Verification run (read-only):
1) docs/SECURITY.md:95-98 (new bullet, git diff shows 14 insertions, none to src/): "re-established at EVERY point of use — pipeline init and the executor `$npm` injection, immediately before the isolation flags are appended".
2) Sub-claim 1 CONFIRMED: apps/cli/src/pipeline.ts:102 `fs.writeFileSync(path.join(WS,'empty.npmrc'),'')` sits in workspace-creation code (fresh timestamped WS dir); no `--userconfig` is consumed and no isolation flags are appended at or near it (the install flags are appended only in the executor). The code's own comment at packages/runner/executor/src/index.ts:757-760 says "Workspace init CREATED it empty" — creation, not re-establishment — so even a charitable reading makes "re-established at ... pipeline init, immediately before the isolation flags are appended" false for that slot.
3) Sub-claim 2 CONFIRMED: the second true point of use is unnamed. apps/cli/src/pipeline.ts:597 re-establishes the file and :601 consumes it via '--userconfig' in the treeHash `npm ls` argv; the in-code comment at :594-596 ("same re-establish contract as the executor install path") and — decisively — the original F6e fix commit cbd8dc4's own message ("the tree-hash npm ls path does the same") show the project itself counts this as a distinct re-establishment site. The SECURITY.md bullet enumerating "EVERY point of use" omits it while naming a non-use site.
4) Sweep re-run over all production src (and dist, and packages/runner/workspace): exactly two `--userconfig` consumers exist (pipeline.ts:601, executor index.ts:764), each with an immediately-preceding writeFileSync('empty.npmrc','') (executor index.ts:761). So the protection claim is true and the finding is correctly self-limited to a mislabel/under-claim of locations — a reader auditing doc-vs-code will find a named site that is not a point of use and a real point of use that is unnamed. Not refuted; one-line doc fix (name the tree-hash `npm ls` site, relabel "pipeline init" as creation) is docs-only and does not touch the frozen src/ fixes.

confirmed.claim: reverify-commands.txt:17-18 — "That is why every log here self-proves its tree with a TREE: line." (and by extension TEST-COUNTING.md's "all re-derived at their stated tree")
confirmed.problem: Mechanically false as written. Only 2 of 27 logs in docs/night-evidence/2026-09-05-F6/ contain a TREE: line (reverify-baseline-34cf515-suite.log:1 and reverify-postchange-suite.log:1). Most importantly reverify-head-suite.log — the independent re-run the report (line 139) and TEST-COUNTING.md (line 58) lean on to confirm the central 472/71/472/0/0/0 figure AT d327e71 — has NO TREE: line, so its d327e71 attribution rests purely on prose. This is exactly the disclosed mishap class (unpinned count after a cwd reset) that the re-derivation ceremony was invented to eliminate, and the run that produced it happened AFTER that lesson. By the convention's own rule "Never trust an unpinned count", an auditor cannot recover the tree of the head-reconfirm from the log itself.
confirmed.evidence: grep -ran "^TREE:" docs/night-evidence/2026-09-05-F6/ -> only reverify-baseline-34cf515-suite.log:1 and reverify-postchange-suite.log:1; head -1 reverify-head-suite.log is test output, no TREE/commit marker.

verdict.reasoning: Discrepancy reproduced; finding stands. (1) Re-ran `grep -ran "^TREE:" docs/night-evidence/2026-09-05-F6/` in the worktree: exactly 2 matches in 27 files — reverify-baseline-34cf515-suite.log:1 and reverify-postchange-suite.log:1, exactly as the finding claims. (2) reverify-commands.txt (actual text at lines 16-18, reviewer's 17-18 is an off-by-one on the same sentence) states unconditionally: "That is why every log here self-proves its tree with a TREE: line. Never trust an unpinned count." That sentence is mechanically false as written — "here" is this directory, and 25 of 27 exported files (all night-run logs, reverify-head-suite.log, reverify-f6a-skip-probe.log, reverify-f6a-ci-sentinel-fail.log) contain no TREE: line. (3) Critically, reverify-head-suite.log has NO self-proving marker of any kind: `grep -an "TREE|d327e71|rev-parse|pwd|/c/Users|C:\\Users"` over the whole 631-line log returns zero hits — its d327e71 attribution rests purely on the surrounding prose, and it was produced by the section-2 command, i.e. AFTER the disclosed cwd-reset mishap that motivated the TREE convention, yet the section-2 recipe (`cd ... && npm test`) omits the `{ echo "TREE: $(git rev-parse HEAD) @ $(pwd)" }` wrapper that sections 1 and 3 use. (4) The doc dependencies are real: NIGHT-F6-HARDENING-2026-09-05.md:136-139 cites "reverify-head-suite.log" as the independent post-audit re-run for the central 472/71/472/0/0/0 figure, and TEST-COUNTING.md:53 header "all re-derived at their stated tree" is self-proven only for the 34cf515 and d327e71+sentinel rows — the `d327e71 (night F6 final)` row's two logs (final-full-suite.log, reverify-head-suite.log) both lack TREE: lines. Checked the natural refutations and none hold: no qualifier elsewhere in the README/errata scopes the "every log" claim; a re-derivation-ceremony-only reading still fails since 3 of 5 reverify logs lack TREE:; the byte-agreement of the two 472 logs (verified: identical result lines, only durations/EXIT differ) proves the count is stable, not the tree attribution — final-full-suite.log itself carries no tree marker either, and the DONE file's final_head line pins the directory, not that log. By the convention's own rule ("Never trust an unpinned count"), an auditor cannot recover the tree of the head-reconfirm from the log itself. This is squarely in scope (docs under review, no production code involved) and exactly the failure class the corrections section claims to have eliminated.
